>
> Another simpler approach that comes to my mind, a more... heuristic approach, would be to run the model in steps. For instance, let's say that the selected simulation time is 5000. So the web interface would show: 0%, 20%, 40%... The penalty in terms of total execution time should be very small.

messages.body_plain:
Nice. I'll give that a try and see what happens.

The model is on a public URL, it's available as a permanent link for use anywhere.

An interesting note if one intends to use shiny with simmer, they don't play well together. One needs an adapter layer that simply copies all the values over into another object of inputs to feed to simmer. Then shiny sees all the values as used. Shiny does some deep inspection of values and how they are used later to detect when to fire events. simmer when using variables does something that shiny doesn't see and core events don't fire.

messages.subject: Using now(env) in mclapply{} and wrap()
messages.subject_clean: Using now(env) in mclapply{} and wrap()
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bart and Iñaki,

I absolutely love the simmer-package. However, I've run into a problem I cannot solve.
I am currently simulating the queue for an outpatient clinic in order to investigate the acces time for new patients. The waiting time for patients that visit regularly is not interesting. After all, it's not weird that a regular patient has to wait half a year for a new appointment, if there is no medical necessity to see him earlier. However, those patients do make us of the same resources (i.e. doctors). I've carried this out by a timeout of the average time between repetitive consultations and then setting the prioritization of a regular patient higher than a new patient.

In order to keep track of the waiting time for a new patient, I've set attributes that appoint the Starting time of the queuing of a patient and the waiting time of the patient, by using now(env) - Starting time.
Below, one can find my (adapted) code.

patientpath <- trajectory("Patients' path")  %>%
  set_attribute("Starttime", function() now(env)) %>%
  log_("Patient waits") %>%
  seize("doctor") %>%
  set_attribute("waitingtime", function(attr) abs(now(env) - attr[["Starttime"]])) %>%
  log_("Start appointment") %>%
  timeout(function() 3) %>%
  log_("End appointment") %>%
  release("doctor") %>%
  branch(option = function() sample(c(0,1), 1, prob = c(1-0.73, 0.73)), continue = c(F),
         trajectory("")  %>%
           log_("No other appointments necessary")
         ) %>%
  log_("Another appointment necessary")  %>%
  timeout(function() 2)%>%
  set_prioritization(values = c(3, 7, TRUE))  %>%
  seize("doctor")%>%
  log_("Start appointment") %>%
  timeout(function() 1)%>% #
  log_("End appointment") %>%
  release("doctor")  %>%
  rollback(9, Inf)

env <- simmer() %>%
    add_resource("doctor", capacity = 2) %>%
    add_generator("person", patientpath, at(0:10), mon = 2)

env  %>% run(50)

Whenever I run it once, no problems occur. However, when I run it multiple times, by using mclappy and wrap(), the simulation doesn't know what to do with now(env), since env has become a list.

My question here is twofold:

Is there a way in which I can investigate the queue of only the new patients without the use of now()? (I’ve tried join(), without success)

Can I use mclapply and now() somehow at the same time?

Thanks in advance,

Dominique

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Using now(env) in mclapply{} and wrap()
messages.subject_clean: [simmer-devel] Using now(env) in mclapply{} and wrap()
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dominique,

> My question here is twofold:
>
> Is there a way in which I can investigate the queue of only the new patients without the use of now()? (I’ve tried join(), without success)

Yes, there is. You just need to extract the arrivals per resource. This data frame contains all access to resources. Given that you are interested in the first-timers, you need to keep the first appearance of each person, filtering out everything else. In dplyr terms,
library(dplyr)

waiting_time <- get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource=TRUE) %>%
  group_by(replication, name) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  transmute(waiting_time = end_time - start_time - activity_time)

> Can I use mclapply and now() somehow at the same time?

Given my first answer, you don’t need now() anymore, but yes, you can. You just need to enclose your whole simulation inside the function you pass to mclapply, including the trajectory. Why? Because it is calling now(env), so that the env should be defined in the same level as the trajectory itself. For instance:
my_simulation <- function(i) {
  patientpath <- trajectory("Patients' path")  %>%
    set_attribute("Starttime", function() now(env)) %>%
    ...

  env <- simmer() %>%
    add_resource("doctor", capacity = 2) %>%
    add_generator("person", patientpath, at(0:10), mon = 2

)

  env %>%
    run(50) %>%
    wrap()
}

envs <- mclapply(1:100, my_simulation)

Regards,
​
--
Iñaki Úcar

messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I'm new to this group, just joined. Wonderful package!

My question:
I want to be able to control/modify the resource capacity inside trajectory as a function of queue length (and eventually, of wait time)

The following (simplified) code below does not work.  -  When I try to call get_mon_resources(simStore) inside the function, it returns empty data-frame and the code crashes with the error:
Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) :
  Expecting a single value: [extent=0].

What am I doing wrong? - Thank you for your help.

simStore <- simmer()

fUpdateNumberOfCashiers <- function() {
  dtLastRes <- simStore %>% get_mon_resources  %>% tail(1)
  nCapacityNow <- dtLastRes$capacity # same as get_capacity(simStore),
  nQueueNow <- dtLastRes$queue       # same as get_queue_count(simStore)

  print(dtLastRes)                  # prints empty data-frame !
  return (as.integer(nQueueNow/4))  # crashes here !
}

trajClient <- trajectory("Client's path") %>%
  log_("Arrived to cashier") %>%
  set_capacity("Cashier", value = fUpdateNumberOfCashiers ) %>%     # crashes here !
  seize("Cashier") %>%
  log_( function(attr) { sprintf("Waited : %.2f mins", now(simStore) - attr["start_time"])}) %>%
  timeout(function() {rexp(1, 30)}) %>%    # One Casier processes 30 clients / hour
  release("Cashier") %>%
  log_(function(attr) { sprintf("In total spent %.2f", now(simStore) - attr["start_time"])})

simStore <- simmer("Store") %>%
  add_resource("Cashier", 1) %>%
  add_generator("Store Clients", trajClient,  function() {rexp(1, 120)}) %>% # 120 clients / hour
  run(until=nHoursObserved <- 1) ; simStore

Op maandag 26 juni 2017 17:40:21 UTC+2 schreef Iñaki Úcar:

> Hi Dominique,
>
> > My question here is twofold:
> >
> > Is there a way in which I can investigate the queue of only the new patients without the use of now()? (I’ve tried join(), without success)
>
> Yes, there is. You just need to extract the arrivals per resource. This data frame contains all access to resources. Given that you are interested in the first-timers, you need to keep the first appearance of each person, filtering out everything else. In dplyr terms,
> library(dplyr)
>
> waiting_time <- get_mon_arrivals(env, per_resource=TRUE) %>%
>   group_by(replication, name) %>%
>   slice(1) %>%
>   transmute(waiting_time = end_time - start_time - activity_time)
>
> > Can I use mclapply and now() somehow at the same time?
>
> Given my first answer, you don’t need now() anymore, but yes, you can. You just need to enclose your whole simulation inside the function you pass to mclapply, including the trajectory. Why? Because it is calling now(env), so that the env should be defined in the same level as the trajectory itself. For instance:
> my_simulation <- function(i) {
>   patientpath <- trajectory("Patients' path")  %>%
>     set_attribute("Starttime", function() now(env)) %>%
>     ...
>
>   env <- simmer() %>%
>     add_resource("doctor", capacity = 2) %>%
>     add_generator("person", patientpath, at(0:10), mon = 2)
>
>   env %>%
>     run(50) %>%
>     wrap()
> }
>
> envs <- mclapply(1:100, my_simulation)
>
> Regards,
> ​
> --
> Iñaki Úcar
> http://www.enchufa2.es
> @Enchufa2 <https://twitter.com/#%21/Enchufa2>

2017-06-28 5:47 GMT+02:00 <sum...@hover.to>:
> What is the easiest way to create an arrival generator function that is off for ten hours and on for 14 hours?

Take a look at the from_to() convenience function. You can specify a distribution, a start_time, a stop_time and a period, e.g. every=24 hours. You'll find a complete example here <https://www.enchufa2.es/archives/simmer-3-6-1.html>.

> Alternatively, what is the easiest way to create an arrival generator function that is defined by rexp, but where the mean arrival rate differs by hour?

If you called your simulation environment "env <- simmer()", you can define your arrival rate as a function of the simulation time, which can be retrieved with now(env).

--

Inaki,Thanks again for your ideas and package.
I spent a few more days and finally got the problem resolved !  But interestingly enough,  the problem has  nothing to do with my original code (which essentially mimics the code from Bank Tutorial (section "One Service counter")),
i.e. all of these don't cause the code crash:
using <- instead of %>%,
not checking special cases for empty data.frames,
initializing simStore variable twice.

What causes the problem is that  the other package (lubridate) masks objects from "simmer", as written seen below

Attaching package: ‘lubridate’
The following objects are masked from ‘package:simmer’:
    now, rollback

Once I replaced
library(simmer); library(lubridate);
with
library(lubridate); library(simmer);

The problem disappeared!

I'll go ahead to post the solution at stackpoverflow, in case anyone else has the same problem.
Cheers
Dmitry
